title: Graves’ disease: thyroid and eye care
intro: Graves’ disease is an autoimmune condition that can make the thyroid produce excess hormone. It may cause palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor and weight loss; eye problems can occur independently of the degree of thyroid overactivity.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Symptoms can resemble anxiety, but persistent fast heartbeat, muscle weakness and unexplained weight change deserve physical assessment. Eye discomfort, bulging or double vision should be reported rather than assumed to be ordinary irritation.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: Blood tests assess thyroid function and relevant antibodies; imaging is selected when needed. Tell the team about supplements, particularly biotin, which can distort some tests, and any pregnancy plans. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Antithyroid medicines, radioiodine or surgery have different advantages and risks. Radioiodine is unsuitable during pregnancy or breastfeeding and can affect eye disease. Some treatments lead to lifelong thyroid-hormone replacement. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Take medicines consistently and attend blood monitoring. Smoking worsens thyroid eye disease, so seek cessation support. Discuss pregnancy promptly because drug choice and monitoring need specialist adjustment. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Fever or sore throat while taking antithyroid medicine requires immediate medical advice and an urgent blood-count safety assessment; follow the drug’s stop-and-contact instructions. Sudden vision loss, severe eye pain, confusion or marked illness with racing heart needs urgent care.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira has tremor and weight loss previously attributed to stress. She describes the full pattern and has thyroid assessment rather than relying only on relaxation.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben develops a sore throat on antithyroid treatment. He follows the written safety plan and contacts the team immediately instead of waiting for routine tests.
